q:

options.A: 1 only

options.D: Half of the cost of the land for the siding

options.A: Expenditure sanction, then administrative approval, then technical sanction

options.D: Administrative approval, then expenditure sanction, then preparation of the detailed estimate

q:
Consider the following statements:

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.A: An offer

options.A: One year

options.A: Chief Administrative Officer (Construction)

q: On a delayed work, liquidated damages go on being levied week after week and the contractor contends that they can keep accumulating without any ceiling. Under the General Conditions of Contract, the total liquidated damages leviable under a works contract cannot exceed:

options.A: 75% of the value of the materials

q:
Consider the following statements about mobilisation advance in a works contract:
1. It is ordinarily limited to 10% of the contract value.

Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: For a very large works tender, a tenderer objects that the earnest money demanded works out to far more than the prescribed ceiling. The Earnest Money Deposit required from tenderers in works tenders is subject to a maximum (cap) of:

q: The successful tenderer neither furnishes the Performance Guarantee/Security Deposit within the period stipulated after the issue of the Letter of Acceptance nor seeks any extension. In such a case, the Railways may:

options.C: Furnish the guarantee amount on behalf of the contractor
options.D: Extend the period indefinitely without any condition

options.A: It is not opened, since the financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical/eligibility packets are found acceptable are opened

Consider the following statements about negotiations on a works tender:
1. If the lowest (L1) tenderer does not accept the counter-offer made to him, negotiations may then be held with the next higher (L2) tenderer.

Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.A: Variation
options.B: Deviation

q: An executive proposes to carry out a major change in the scope and design of a sanctioned work first and obtain sanction for the change after the modified work is completed. In respect of a material modification of a sanctioned work, the correct requirement is:

options.A: Sanction of the contractor executing the work
options.B: Sanction only after the whole work is completed
options.C: Approval of the Railway Board in every case, however small the modification
options.D: Prior sanction of the competent authority, with finance concurrence, before the modified portion of the work is executed

q: During a periodic check, a difference is noticed between the expenditure shown against a work in the executive office register and the figure booked for the same work in the accounts office. Such differences come to light because the figures entered in the Works Register are:

options.C: Examined for the first time only during audit inspection
options.D: Accepted as correct without any comparison with the accounts figures

options.C: Amounts outstanding for recovery or adjustment in connection with works
options.D: Departmental charges recovered on deposit works

options.A: 1 only

options.D: The order of precedence of the documents laid down in the contract conditions

q: A contractor, without asking the Railway, hands over a portion of his work to another firm to execute. Under the General Conditions of Contract, this is impermissible because a contractor:

options.A: Cannot sublet or assign the work, or any part of it, without the prior written consent of the Railway
options.B: Can sublet the work after merely informing the sectional staff
options.C: Can assign the contract to his creditors at his discretion
options.D: Is free to sublet the entire work to any other contractor

q: In the contract documents for a work, references to the 'Engineer' are to be understood as references to:

options.A: Any engineer employed by the contractor
options.B: The engineer who prepared the abstract estimate
options.C: The officer designated in the contract under whose supervision and direction the work is to be executed
options.D: The Chief Engineer of the Railway Board

q: The successful tenderer receives the Letter of Acceptance but the formal agreement is yet to be signed, and he asks whether any contract exists at all. The correct position is that the Letter of Acceptance:

options.A: Is a mere formality with no legal effect
options.B: Communicates acceptance of his tender and brings the contract into existence, even before the formal agreement is executed
options.C: Entitles him to payment in advance for the whole work
options.D: Replaces the need for security deposit in all cases

q: A change ordered in a contract is so extensive that the work as changed bears little resemblance to the work originally contracted for. Such a change, which alters the entire character of the contract, is described as:

options.A: A deviation
options.B: An extra item
options.D: Vitiation of the contract

q: A contractor abandons a work midway and the contract is terminated for his default. The Railway gets the remaining work completed through another agency, and the extra cost so incurred is borne:

options.A: At the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor
options.B: Wholly by the Railways in every case
options.C: By the tender committee that awarded the original contract
options.D: By the new agency as a goodwill gesture

q: Completion of a work is delayed because the Railway itself failed to hand over the site and to supply departmental materials in time. In such a case, extension of the completion period can be granted because the delay:

options.A: Is claimed by the contractor as a matter of right for any reason
options.B: Is entirely due to the neglect of the contractor
options.C: Is due to causes beyond the control of the contractor
options.D: Can never be granted under the General Conditions of Contract

q: Soon after a completed work is handed over, defects appear in it during the maintenance period. Under the contract, these defects are required to be:

options.A: Repaired by the Railway at its own cost in all cases
options.B: Made good by the contractor at his own cost
options.C: Ignored until the work is taken up again for repairs
options.D: Charged to the contractor's security deposit without any notice to him

q: Under an item-rate contract, the quantity of an item actually executed turns out to be more than the quantity shown in the schedule. The contractor is paid:

options.A: A lump sum for the whole work, irrespective of quantities
options.B: On a cost-plus basis
options.C: Only for the scheduled quantity, whatever was actually executed
options.D: For the actual quantities of each item executed, at the rates quoted by him for those items

q: In a tender invited under the two-packet system, the financial packet of a tenderer is opened at the first stage itself along with his technical packet. This procedure is wrong because in this system:

options.A: The financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical packets are found acceptable are opened
options.B: The technical packet is opened only after the contract is awarded
options.C: Two separate contracts are awarded for one work
options.D: The financial packet is opened first and the technical packet later

q: Rates received for a work are high and negotiations with tenderers become unavoidable. As a rule, such negotiations are to be held:

options.A: With all the tenderers one by one
options.B: With the highest tenderer
options.D: With the tenderer recommended by the executive

q: A tender committee is constituted to examine the tenders received for a work. Such a committee normally comprises:

options.A: Only the executive officer dealing with the work
options.B: The executive officer, the finance/accounts officer and an officer of another department
options.C: The General Manager and the Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Representatives of the tenderers

q: In the deliberations of a tender committee, the finance member's distinctive contribution is to:

options.A: Prepare the tender documents
options.B: Execute the work after it is awarded
options.C: Inspect the work during its execution
options.D: See that the tender is financially sound, funds are available and financial propriety is observed

q: For a tender of low value, the accepting authority proposes to accept it on its own without placing it before a tender committee. This course, where permissible for tenders of low value, is known as:

options.A: Direct acceptance
options.B: Single tendering
options.D: Post-facto acceptance
